# ADR 0002 â€” Export a plain text summary

## Context

Input records held by the system need a representation that can be read,
copied and compared without any special viewer. The simplest such
representation is plain text: one record per line, in the order the
records were supplied. Fixing that representation as a decision â€” rather
than leaving each caller to invent its own â€” keeps exported summaries
comparable with one another, and keeps the behaviour testable in terms
of the input alone.

Two forces shape the answer. First, the export must not reorder or
reinterpret what it is given: the order of the input is information, so
the export preserves it rather than imposing an order of its own.
Second, the export must be faithful to the characters it receives,
including non-ASCII ones, so that summaries of internationalised content
survive the round trip unaltered.

## Capability statement

The system must be able to export a set of input records as a plain text
summary, in which each record appears as one line and the lines appear in
the order the records were supplied. The export is a pure rendering of
its input: it applies no sorting, no formatting options and no
transformation of record content, and it preserves the characters of each
record exactly, including Unicode characters outside ASCII. An empty set
of input records is a valid input and produces an empty summary.

## User stories / scenarios

- As a consumer of the export, I want records rendered one per line in
  their original order, so that the summary matches the sequence I
  supplied and can be compared line by line.
- As a consumer handling internationalised records, I want the exported
  characters preserved exactly, so that non-ASCII content is not lost or
  mangled by the export.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The output preserves the input order, as one record per line.
2. An empty input yields an empty string.
3. Unicode characters are preserved.

## Out of scope

- Any new runtime implementation â€” this decision records the required
  behaviour only; no implementing code is authorised by it.
- Sorting or any other reordering of the records.
- Formatting options, configuration or alternative output formats: the
  output format is plain text.
- User interface surfaces for the export.
- Network delivery or transport of the exported summary.

## Open questions

- None.
